original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-rh}
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of smooth proper curves
over a field $k$ which satisfies the equivalent conditions of
Lemma \ref{lemma-generically-etale}. If
$k = H^0(Y, \mathcal{O}_Y) = H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$
and $X$ and $Y$ have genus $g_X$ and $g_Y$, then
$$
2g_X - 2 = (2g_Y - 2) \deg(f) + \deg(R)
$$
where $R \subset X$ is the effective Cartier divisor cut out by
the different of $f$.

The residue separability is essential and preserved.
statement:
A curve over a field $k$ means an integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type and Krull dimension $1$. A normal (equivalently, nonsingular or regular) curve has regular local rings; its local rings at closed points are discrete valuation rings. A rational map of integral $k$-varieties is an equivalence class of morphisms defined on dense open subschemes, and it is dominant if it maps generic points to generic points. A proper normal curve has a unique nonsingular projective model (the regular proper curve with the same function field). The function field of a curve $X$ is $k(X)=\kappa(\eta_X)$.

Let $X \to \Spec(k)$ be smooth of relative dimension $1$ at a closed
point $x \in X$. If $\kappa(x)$ is separable over $k$, then for
any uniformizer $s$ in the discrete valuation ring $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$
the element $\text{d}s$ freely generates $\Omega_{X/k, x}$
over $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-uniformizer-works}
Let $X \to \Spec(k)$ be smooth of relative dimension $1$ at a closed
point $x \in X$. If $\kappa(x)$ is separable over $k$, then for
any uniformizer $s$ in the discrete valuation ring $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$
the element $\text{d}s$ freely generates $\Omega_{X/k, x}$
over $\mathcal{O}_{X, x}$.
